image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align above the orange can for a tactile lift test; fill state is not visually identifiable.
Descend with open jaws around the orange can's upper body, maintaining a vertical grasp.
Close gradually to establish bilateral touch on the orange can before testing its load.
Lift the orange can slightly while holding the opening fixed; inspect retention and tactile load deformation.
Orange is retained, but touch alone is ambiguous; return it to the table before comparing the blue can under the same grasp.
Release the supported orange can and withdraw vertically to clear it before testing the blue can.
Translate above the blue can with the jaws open and fingertips clear of both lids.
Lower open jaws around the blue can to the same upper-body contact height used for the orange can.
Establish bilateral tactile contact on the blue can with gradual jaw closure, holding the arm still.
Lift the blue can slightly at fixed opening to observe tactile loading and visual retention for comparison.
Blue is retained, but its load cue is uncertain. Set it down to obtain a directly comparable orange tactile observation.
Release the supported blue can and raise the empty jaws clear of its lid.
Return above the orange can for the comparison touch, keeping the fingers above both cans.
Descend to the orange can's upper sidewall for a controlled tactile comparison.
Close to a reproducible opening and record the orange can's supported tactile contact before loading it.
Lift orange by 6 cm at fixed opening, using changes in the tactile contact under load to assess whether it is empty.
Orange retained with an upward tactile boundary shift under load. Return it safely and compare blue's supported-to-lifted deformation before selection.
Move to the blue can with open jaws, retaining safe clearance above both cans for a matched tactile test.
Lower to the matched grasp height and close on blue; record supported tactile geometry before the final comparative lift.
Let blue's contact settle, then lift 6 cm at fixed opening to compare its tactile loading with orange's broad, slightly shifted contact.
Blue shows larger tactile boundary motion under the lift than orange, suggesting more load. Return blue to the table and select the apparently lighter orange can.
Withdraw from the released blue can and return above orange with open fingers and lid clearance.
Regrasp the orange can, selected as lighter from the comparative tactile loading, for transfer to the basket.
Lift the selected orange can vertically to clear the basket rim, maintaining the established grasp.
Carry the visibly retained orange can left over the basket opening, keeping its base above the rim.
Orange is centered over the basket opening. Open the jaws to release it while holding the arm stationary.
The released orange can is descending inside the basket. Hold clear with open jaws while it settles.
Orange appears settled inside the basket with no tactile contact. Withdraw the open gripper upward and toward the clear center.
Hold safely clear while observing the orange can resting inside the basket; the blue can remains on the table.
Maintain the open gripper clear of the basket and preserve the settled placement.
Hold clear; the selected orange can remains in the basket and the blue can stays on the table.
Keep the arm safely clear and maintain the observed placement without disturbing either can.
Hold clear with open jaws; the selected orange can remains visibly inside the basket.
Maintain safe clearance and preserve the observed placement of the selected can inside the basket.
Keep the open gripper clear; the selected orange can remains in the basket and the other can is undisturbed.
Preserve the observed placement and hold safely clear with open jaws.
Hold clear of the settled orange can in the basket without disturbing the remaining can.
Maintain safe clearance and preserve the selected can's placement inside the basket.
Hold open and clear; orange remains visibly inside the basket and blue remains on the table.
Maintain clearance and leave the selected can undisturbed inside the basket.
